newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Petrobras mum on oil imports.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Petrobras mum on oil imports.

text.p: Brazilian state oil firm Petrobras Wednesday declined to comment on differences between officially registered fuel imports in January and its own stated purchases.
"We have been instructed not to comment," a spokesman said.
The government delayed the announcement of January's trade balance because of doubts about fuel and lubricant imports.

It said Petrobras reported fuel and lubricant imports of $650 million during January but the SISCOMEX import registration system only registered $61.4 million, well down on average fuel imports seen since last September.
A joint Finance and Industry and Commerce Ministry statement said the inconsistency with Petrobras imports was the only irregularity it had identified in January's trade figures.
Everardo Maciel, head of the Internal Revenue Service, said according to the local Invest News agency that it was up to Petrobras to explain why its imports did not get registered.
He said it was possible that fuel unloaded into onshore tanks in Petrobras complexes did not count as physical imports even though it was on Brazilian territory.
Luiz Furlan, president of meatpackers Sadia and foreign trade representative of Sao Paulo's Fiesp industrial association, said Petrobras' post-customs procedures were probably to blame.

He defended the SISCOMEX system against its critics, saying it would guarantee greater transparency in government trade statistics and predicting that all teething problems would be overcome at the end of the first quarter.
"It's a new system so problems are only to be expected," he said.
